text:
The Hurricanes leave for Finland on top of the NHL, 14-3-2 after running the Blackhawks over 9-2, and nothing about it smells like a fluke. They take 58 percent of the expected goals at five on five (expected goals measure the quality of chances), among the best shares anywhere, and our race simulations give them a 99 percent shot at the playoffs and 76 percent at the Metropolitan Division.

The story that keeps writing itself is depth. Jordan Staal is out, and Mark Jankowski, a journeyman on most of his stops, has six points in his last ten while the New York Times wrote that he has "Conn Smythe shoes to fill." Logan Stankoven has 12 points in ten, Jesperi Kotkaniemi seven. All three are running ahead of their chances, so expect some cooling. Sebastian Aho just passed Eric Staal in two franchise categories, and the Carrier, Aho and Svechnikov line has outscored teams 12-6.

Pyotr Kochetkov is the piece that makes it scary. His first loss of the season came in Nashville, but he has saved 5.2 goals more than expected over his last five starts. If you're looking for a worry, it's that Carolina's goals are running about four ahead of its chances. That's a small tax on a very good team.
headline: Carolina is the best team in hockey, and it isn't close
